observations.behavior: Gray pointer disk on right travels toward the1PM row, stretches into a wide rounded bar, then becomes a thin horizontal insertion guide. Calendar has1–5PM rows.
Blue outlined press ring appears, grows and begins a downward drag while the horizontal guide follows with lag.

Blue event block grows downward from1PM; text advances in15-minute steps to3PM. Title New Event is clipped until height becomes sufficient. Pointer/guide positions remain independent of snapping text.
Event and press ring fade away on release; thin gray guide remains.
Guide moves downward from3PM to4PM. New press ring appears around148 and moves upward.
Second block grows upward from4PM. Label first3:30PM–4PM, then3:15PM–4PM. Top boundary and guide track smoothly with spring-like settling; text remains quantized.
Release fades event and ring. Gray insertion guide slides upward toward3PM.
Third press ring appears at3PM and begins downward movement.
Thin3PM–3:15PM block appears below3PM. New Event stays clipped in the short interval.
Drag crosses its starting point; interval briefly reads3PM–3PM, bar stays visibly rounded at minimum height rather than disappearing.
Block reverses and grows above3PM through2:45,2:30,2:15,2PM,1:45,1:30. Ring and guide continue to lead the smoothed event boundary.
Release fades block, guide travels downward again.
Fourth event grows downward from3:15PM to5PM, changing duration in15-minute steps and revealing New Event as height increases.
Event/ring fade. Guide holds at5PM, then begins moving right.
Thin guide shrinks through rounded wide bar back into a circular pointer as it exits right.
Gray disk moves slightly downward outside the grid and rests; source ends without returning to the exact initial pointer position.

distinctness: Cursor disk morphs into an insertion guide and event grows in either direction across a zero-duration crossing. Treat all four drags as one example. Clean original vector/type reconstruction feasible; lower visual spectacle than printer/Ringwriter.
limits: Do not infer an off-axis precision interaction: the observed clip demonstrates vertical calendar-event creation; no horizontal distance-to-precision mapping is shown.
